original.title: The Discovery of Grounded Theory
original.note: Record dated 2017 (Routledge reissue of the 1967 book).

core_idea: A research methodology for building theory from data rather than testing existing theory. Researchers collect and analyse data at the same time, compare constantly between data and emerging categories, sample theoretically to develop categories, and stop when categories are saturated.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: What is going on in a setting that existing theory doesn't explain well?
How do people manage a process or problem (e.g. becoming a migrant student, coping with a reform)?
Typical data: interviews, observation, documents, analysed through coding and memo writing.
common_mistakes: Starting with a full theoretical framework and then claiming the theory 'emerged'.
Not saying which version you follow (Glaser, Strauss & Corbin, Charmaz).
